statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail holds in the low band because NQ trades 29,608.50, roughly 156 points below the 29,764.25 overnight high after a genuine retracement, while ES is -0.24% and YM -0.76%. Stress moves up within the high band as WTI prints three-month highs near $94.21, Brent trades close to $100 and the 10-year sits near 4.78%.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping resolves to EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD alike, and Tail remains far below the block threshold. A narrow danger window is flagged for the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC, where a single auction discounts three calendar days of Gulf, energy and rates news. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds 29,608.50 inside a two-way overnight band while Dow futures fall 0.76% and WTI prints three-month highs before the post-holiday U.S. reopening
body:
U.S. cash equity markets were closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30 UTC today, so the Nasdaq-100 last settled a full cash session on 4 September at 29,544.15. NQ futures trade at 29,608.50, up 43.25 points or 0.15% from the 29,565.25 previous close, inside an overnight band of 29,525.00-29,764.25. The structural fact that carries this assessment is where price sits within that band: NQ tagged 29,764.25 earlier in the session and has since given back roughly 156 points, leaving it only about 84 points above the overnight low. That is a deep, completed retracement rather than a shallow-pullback sequence, and there is no failed-retracement chain, no repeated extension and no holding near a session extreme. It is the single strongest argument for keeping Tail near its base rate.

Cross-asset confirmation is not merely absent, it is contradictory. S&P 500 futures trade at 7,703.25, down 18.75 points or 0.24%, in a 7,694.75-7,728.50 band, and Dow futures are at 53,036.00, down 404.00 points or 0.76%, in a 52,958.00-53,336.00 band. A tape in which NQ is modestly higher, ES is down a quarter percent and YM is down three quarters of a percent is a rotation, not an index-wide directional move, and it does not support a trend-up or trend-down label.

The Stress side has strengthened again. WTI trades at $94.16, up 2.93% on the day and within five cents of its $94.21 session high, a three-month high, with Brent above $97 and approaching $100. The driver is the Strait of Hormuz corridor: the U.S. struck three Iranian tankers over the weekend, the IRGC claimed strikes on tankers and U.S.-linked vessels, Saudi Aramco's Jizan refinery was hit for the second time in a month, and Iran has said an agreement with Oman to manage shipping through the strait is nearing completion. Transit has thinned to roughly ten commodity ships a day over the past ten days, although about seven million barrels a day of crude and products still flow. That energy channel feeds a rates path that was already hawkish: August payrolls printed 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3%, which lifted market-implied odds of a 25 basis point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC to roughly 59%. The 10-year Treasury yield last settled near 4.78% and the 2-year near 4.34%. Against all of that, VIX at 15.30 is historically low, which is why Stress sits in the lower half of the high band rather than higher.

The evidence therefore separates cleanly. The macro environment is difficult and the headline stack is dense, which is a Stress and Confidence matter. The observed price path is two-way, deeply retracing and internally conflicted, which is a Tail matter and argues for a low reading. The one genuine structural risk inside the next 24 hours is the 13:30 UTC cash reopening, where a single auction must discount three days of accumulated news; that is expressed as a narrow danger window and a conditional forecast peak of 14 in the 14:00 UTC hour, not as a claim that a directional path has been observed.

Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run, but its collection timestamp was 2026-09-08T02:19:06Z, more than five hours old and outside the 90-minute freshness window, so it was treated as stale and used for discovery only. Every price, yield, oil and volatility figure above comes from independent current research against primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment and every one of them mapped to EA_ON. Tail sat at 5-6 through the European and early U.S. hours of 7 September, stepped to 9-10 around the 14:00 and 16:00 UTC windows, fell back to 5 into the Labor Day evening, then held a persistent 6-10 range from 22:00 UTC onward as the overnight NQ advance built to 29,764.25 and was then given back. Stress climbed from the mid-50s into a 62-65 range once the weekend Gulf escalation and the crude move were priced, and Confidence recovered from 75 to 85 as live futures evidence displaced the holiday-thinned reads. Dominant mode alternated between normal and mixed and never resolved to a trend label.
outlookSummary: The projection holds Tail inside the low band across all 24 hours, with a shallow rise into the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening and a peak of 14 in the 14:00 UTC hour that still maps to EA_ON. That rise is conditional structural risk from an unusually information-dense reopening auction, not an assertion that a directional path has been observed. Stress runs 63-71, highest across the U.S. cash session, on the unresolved Gulf energy channel, a 4.78% 10-year and roughly 59% implied odds of a September rate increase. Confidence decays from 85 to 61 with distance from the evidence. The stated invalidations are a reclaim of 29,764.25 with no retracement, a European-led break below 29,525.00 that holds, or repeated extension after failed retracements once U.S. cash trades; any of those would justify a materially higher Tail than projected here.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NQ trades 29,608.50, +0.15%, inside a 29,525.00-29,764.25 overnight band and roughly 156 points below that high after a genuine retracement. ES is -0.24% and YM -0.76%, a split tape rather than an index trend, so Tail stays low while Stress rises on crude at three-month highs.
